# Positions of Large Groups. The pairs must come in increasing order of start.

@example The groups are "h", "aaa", "pp" and "yyy"; "pp" has only two letters.
"haaappyyy"
=> [[1,3],[6,8]]

@example Three letters are doubled, but no letter appears three times in a row.
"bookkeeper"
=> []

@example The four m's make one group, which runs to the end of the string.
"hmmmm"
=> [[1,4]]

# Too short for a large group.
"a"
=> []

"qq"
=> []

# Exactly 3 letters is large: here the whole string.
"ttt"
=> [[0,2]]

# A large group at the start.
"eeek"
=> [[0,2]]

# A large group that ends at the last letter.
"xyzzz"
=> [[2,4]]

# The same letter in two separate groups: they are not merged.
"kkkkdkkk"
=> [[0,3],[5,7]]

# Large groups back to back.
"cccbbbddd"
=> [[0,2],[3,5],[6,8]]

# Groups of two between the large ones.
"aabbbccdddd"
=> [[2,4],[7,10]]

# Alternating letters: every group has one letter.
"ababab"
=> []

# Nine equal letters are one group, not three groups of three.
"wwwwwwwww"
=> [[0,8]]

# A group of 256 letters: its length counted in an unsigned char wraps
# to 0.
"jwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwjjj"
=> [[1,256],[257,259]]

# One letter 1000 times: indices past 255.
""
=> [[0,999]]

# left over at the end.
""
